A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JointDiT and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–C. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original joint-generation, depth-estimation, and depth-conditioned generation results, including component ablations and supplementary image-quality and LoRA-rank experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports feature visualizations, expanded baseline comparisons, and qualitative failure analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 revises the specified timestep sampler to one minus v2's transform, retaining the mixture probabilities and other core method components. This changes the written sampling rule; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation or training runs changed.

E1.justification: The training datasets and named evaluation benchmarks are retained. Qualitative coverage expands to explicit pixel-art scenarios in Figures 2, 6, and 12; v2 already included cartoon and realistic examples, so illustration coverage is not entirely new. Pexel becoming Pexels is a naming correction.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially broadens comparison to multitask models by adding 4M-21, MultiMAE, Unified-IO, and Unified-IO 2 across five depth datasets. It also fills the previously absent Depth-Anything-V2 ScanNet comparison. Depth-Anything-V2 additionally participates in the supplementary 3D-lifting comparison.

E3.justification: v2's blanket LoRA-rank-64 statement becomes rank 64 for DiT blocks and ranks 512 or 1024 for the input stage. The new feature-analysis protocol uses 50 generated samples per domain, features at t = 0.48, and even-index subsampling before PCA. These reported settings do not establish that retained benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantive analysis of RGB/depth branch representations through PCA visualizations in Section 4.4, further 3D-lifting comparisons in Appendix B.1, and mirror failure analysis in Appendix B.4. The existing scheduling, timestep-sampling, LoRA-rank, and panorama analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new PCA analysis's 50 samples per domain describe its sample size, not repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds five-dataset results for four multitask baselines and Depth-Anything-V2 ScanNet values of 4.1 AbsRel and 97.9 delta1. New qualitative findings cover branch-feature differences, stylized geometry, and mirror failures. This substantially expands reported evidence while retaining JointDiT's existing numerical results and the values in Tables 2–4 and 6–8.

T1.justification: Equation (7) changes f(t) from s*sigmoid(z)/(1+(s-1)*sigmoid(z)) to one minus that expression, with unchanged s values. This non-equivalent mathematical correction aligns the sampling bias with Figure 3. Equations (1)–(6) remain unchanged, and no new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: The unified RGB-depth model, two proposed training techniques, and conditional-generation claims are retained. The introduction adds explicit claims about plausible geometry in cartoon/pixel-art domains and complementary specialization of the RGB and depth branches, modestly extending the contribution narrative.

C2.justification: v3 introduces a tentative geometry-versus-texture specialization explanation, replacing Figure 2's attribution of competing methods' rough surfaces to depth-estimation uncertainty. It also explicitly identifies reflective surfaces and mirrors as failure conditions. Existing interpretations involving image priors, teacher-depth quality, and computational overhead remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly specifies input-stage LoRA ranks, alpha equal to half the rank, and a zero-initialized projection after joint attention; A.1 clarifies comparator preprocessing. Conversely, v3 omits the guidance scale of 3.5, BLIP2 prompt extraction for ImageNet/Pexels joint-generation evaluation, and absolute sampling times of 1.6 and 4.7 seconds.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for the four multitask baselines and broadens related work to depth completion, sound-driven visual generation, single-image 3D reconstruction, and texturing. The central positioning of diffusion transformers against prior U-Net-based joint models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and experimental prose receive local tightening and rewrites. Some protocol descriptions move to Appendix A.1, new analysis subsections expand the appendix organization, and acknowledgments are added. The six-section main narrative and most existing exposition retain their structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 6, 7, 9, and 12 for features, 3D comparisons, failures, and illustrations. Figure 2 replaces its portrait comparison with a pixel-art example; Table 1 expands and moves, and Figure 5 contracts to one column. Existing supplementary figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: Expanded baseline comparisons, feature analysis, and explicit mirror failures make the evidence and applicability boundaries more informative. Correcting Equation (7) and documenting LoRA details improve consistency and reproducibility, although omitted guidance, prompt-preparation, and absolute timing details partly offset those gains. Overall, v3 provides a limited quality improvement to a paper whose central claims and headline numerical results remain largely unchanged.
